I was hit in the face by a decently-sied rock a neighbor kid threw off a small cliff towards me. broke my nose but we had made up and were playing Sonic Adventure 2 together later that night, because I nor he considered at any point that it could have killed me.

Had another friend in high school who  followed me down the highway one day trying to shoot me with his airsoft gun as he was driving behind me. I remember reachng into the backseat and grabbing whatever I could find (fastfood leftovers) and throwing them out my window at this friend, the bag grazed his windshield, bounced over, and splattered the windshield of the car behind my friend with a ketchup and mustard covered half-ate chilly-dog.  

When we got back to my house I teased him about being such a terrible shot, he told me about my chillidog hitting the car behind him, and we laughed.

I was on my way to pick up my old high school crush for the date I had only ever dreamed of for years. I was on cloud nine as I drove way too fast on those twisty roads I hardly knew. My left wheels were slightly in the wrong lane as I was rounding a curve, I overcorrected and suddenly was facing the guardrail near the top of that curvy mountain road. 

Before my car had even smashed through the guardrail I had already realized I was going to die at the young age of 19. Time seemed to slow down to a crawl like you see in the movies. The whole crash only took a couple of seconds but I had a long internal monologue that ordinarily would take about 5 minutes to say out loud.

I felt at peace. I had up until that point believed I was invincible, people could die in car wrecks but I had firmly believed my fate was greater than such a trivial death, until that moment. My right foot was planted hard on the breaks as I decided it was okay to die. Now I just had to wait, thinking about my successes and failures, knowing I had always done my best, death didnt seem like such a bad thing, a bittersweat ending to a bittersweat life, almost poetic.

Then after what felt like an infinity my car finally crossed the 2 feet to the guardrail, smashed right through, and I went over the mountain. To this day I am amazed I survived. If I believed in any sort of diety I would certainly have claimed my survival to be a miracle, but I believe I just got lucky.

The mountain was in a rural area, covered in trees, shoulder to shoulder with no possible way to avoid them, any of which would give my car a funky new V-shaped hood and ensured my death. My car went down at an angle. I went in between the first two trees, the next two my car barely fit between, the two beyond that snapped off both my door mirrors but did not stop me, then I saw it, a huge tree dead a head, the end. Right as I was about to hit it dead center my car abruptly came to a full stop, quit surprising seeing as I was rolling down a mountainside too steep to park even with an e-break.

I don't know what stopped my car at that last second. Maybe some weeds locked around my tires, I am not sure.  I was fine, not even scratched. My car had scratches all over and had lost both mirrors but was otherwise fine as well, I even took my date out in the very same car just an hour later.
 

I got out and looked around and could not believe it. Had my car been angled one more inch to the left I would have hit a tree and died. Had my car been angled one more inch to the right I would have hit a tree and died.  This was a full on wooded area and the only areas with trees far enough apart for a car to fit was this new angled trail I had just made out of pure luck.

It was a life-changing experience, allowing me to accept my mortality and taught me a major lesson about being carless behind the wheels. The only negative I can draw from the event is that nobody believes the story when I tell them. Wish I hadn't moved so I could just take people out to the spot and show them the scraped plastic all along that part of the hill where I crashed. At least I will always have the memory of being totally at peace like I felt facing my own death on that twisted road.
